summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for an acute flare of chronic pancreatitis with severe epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and her standard IV pain and anti-nausea regimen. During the admission, she developed a fever, and blood cultures grew Herbaspirillum species, a gram-negative rod likely originating from her port. She was treated with IV antibiotics, initially Zosyn and then switched to ceftazidime based on sensitivities, with concurrent antibiotic dwells into the port. Her pain improved, and she was advanced to a regular diet. Her anemia was addressed with IV iron, and anticoagulation was managed with a Lovenox bridge back to warfarin. She was discharged home with home health services to complete a course of IV ceftazidime and port dwells, along with instructions for INR monitoring and follow-up blood cultures.
